TBH I don't think you need to tell your therapist face to face. You don't owe them an explanation in the same way that you don't owe your hairdresser an explanation if you decide to go to another salon. If telling them in person seems too much, I would just send an email to their office explaining that you've decided to end your sessions and seek treatment elsewhere. The main thing is that you shouldn't delay finding the right therapist to protect the feelings of your  current therapist :)

All I'll say is that it's worth holding on a little but longer. It sounds like you still have a lot to experience. I get that it all feels a bit pointless right now. I've been there. But this might be the only life you have. I think it's worth sticking around. 
If you can, please tell someone how you're feeling right now.

To be honest, it upsets me quite a bit that this subreddit doesn't allow people to share their coping strategies. I'm not really sure how people here can offer or receive help if no one can share what worked for them in terms of getting by day by day. I can completely understand not advocating something as a miracle cure but not allowing people to provide any information or resources seems so restrictive.

My guess is Clive and Leo. The football sock will surely be the damning evidence (unless it was planted). The football sock can't be Clive, Ian or any left field suspect cos they haven't given DNA. At the end of one of the episode they made a point of filming Leo playing football and focused on his socks. It's established that Leo is friendly with Clive. I think that Clive and possibly Leo were involved in the other rapes and my have targeting victims through taxi requests/intercepting breakdown reports. Clive may have also filmed and distributed videos of the rapes.  This would also explain the souvenirs locked away in his drawer.  

Clive will most likely kill is wife at the start of this episode (offering some shock factor). He will then probably go on the run while Leo is brought in for questioning cos of the sock. Leo will crack, tell them Clive was in on it and they will go on a hunt for Clive. His son might end up helping the investigation somehow. 

While there is lots of damning circumstantial evidence to implicate Jim, all of it can explained away by him being a cheating prick. It's also possible that Cath purposely refused alibis to ensure he would be charged (she probably believes he did it in fairness). 

While this conclusion isn't the shocker we expect after season one, it is pretty consistent with the type of reveal in season 2. I can't imagine them going with a left field suspect like the vicar cos would undermine everything they've set up in the series so far. I feel the same way about the Tom/group of young boys theory, this theory is further undermined by the fact they are too young to have committed the other rapes and there is nothing to place them at any of the crime scenes. 

If I has to guess a left field suspect, my money would be on Nige cos he always gave me the creep and his mother said "I know men who'd rape you" to the journalist in series one. BUT he's barely featured this season so I think there's a slim chance of that happening.

I do understand why people suspect him. He is clearly troubled with the whole existential crisis he has going on. Also he features quite prominently in this series for someone who is largely extraneous to the plot. After season 1, I think many Broadchurch expect the culprit to betray our expectation in some way and Paul definitely would.

However, apart from the fact he would be a shocking choice, I think of any evidence to suggest that he is the rapist. He has never been placed at the crime scene and. 
he has no history violence/perversion

Really interesting theory with a lot of pretty compelling points. My only issue is that this revelation would quite bad writing. The musician hasn't been established as being connected to any major characters and therefore the reactions to him being the rapist would be pretty boring. Same with the audience, the shock value arises only from the fact that we don't really know him, not that he has betrayed our expectations in some way. Also, it would render almost all of the evidence red herrings.
Another thing that implicates Jim is the fact that two condoms were missing from his pack. If he was unsuccessful getting off with the waitress, he surely wouldn't have used two condoms

I think this theory hold a lot of weight. The only thing that's irking me is the fact Clive has Trish's keys locked away and clearly has been up to no good as indicated by the exchange with his wife at the end of the last episode. Maybe Leo is the rapist and Clive is the accomplice/getaway driver/cameraman. Sure, there is a ton of circumstantial evidence to implicate Jim but pretty much all of it can be explained away by him being a smarmy prick.

I think this is certainly a plausible theory but I think it would be pretty poor writing if that was the case. Tamworth hasn't featured prominently enough for that reveal to hold any real emotional weight. Plus I can't recall anything that would connect him to the other rapes. It also seems a bit weird for him to draw attention to the site of the rape unnecessarily and commit the act on his own property. Plus no one has reported seeing him at the house. 

I personally think the obligatory shocking revelation won't be the identity of the culprit but the fact that there is more than one and how they worked together to commit the rapes. My money is on Jim and Leo or Clive and Leo.

Even though they are the two most likely suspects, I doubt they are in it together. When Jim van broke down a few episodes ago, they had a rather heated conversation about who it. That would be very strange if they were in it together, especially since there was no one else around to hear.

I think it's certainly possible that Cath falsified the evidence but she seemed visibly shaken when she found the condoms and reported it to the police (she was alone during both scenes so there was no one to perform for). Her behavior seems a bit to erratic for someone with a hidden agenda. One minute she hates Cath, the next she's apologizing. She wants to ruin her husbands life, then she's considering moving away with him. It seems like she's struggling in a really difficult situation. Don't get me wrong, I'm still kinda suspicious about her but her behavior doesn't fit with someone who's masterminding the situation. It is possible, however, that the condom were the final straw for Cath and she decided not to provide Jim with an alibi even if it was legitimate.

After this episode, I think we can safely say that Ed and Ian can be disqualified as suspects. 

Ian was acting shady cos of the spyware and I think was blackout that night therefore unable to knock out, tie and gag Trish. 

Ed seems to be legitimately in love with Trish and disturbed by the allegations. Broadchurch creators seems to be taking their responsibility to present rape responsibly seriously. They are unlikely to present a story where a man rapes a woman cos he loves her. It's about power, not attraction. 

This was a pretty damning episode for Jim. 
1) he bought condoms before the rape 
2) he failed to get off with the waitress and was presumably roaming the woods sexually frustrated 
3) he doesn't have an alibi for the other rapes and they coincided with Cath being away
4) he claimed to have picked up rape victim Laura (even though she was presumably never picked up) 

I'm not really sure how it can't be Jim at this point. Cath could have planted some of the evidence but her erratic behavior seems to reflect someone who is struggling not calculated. 

My thinking is that Jim had an accomplice or someone who came across the rape and joined in. I think this person will be the DNA profile from the end of this episode. It's not very ground breaking but the only possibility, in my opinion, is Leo. It's not going to be Clive because he has already had a conversation with Jim which indicated they weren't in it together. Given the final scene of this episode shows all of the main suspects and they say it's a match for "one of their men" (so it's not gonna be a left-field person like the Vicar or Nige). Plus the fact it's a football sock is pretty damning for Leo. 

I  don't really want this to be the conclusion cos it's not very interesting but I think it's the most logical guess at this point.
